steps.label: Write the numerator as A·Dr′ + B·Dr and equate coefficients
lines: The numerator mixes cosx and sinx, so write

lines.text: it as A times the derivative of the
denominator, plus B times the denominator.

lines: Compare the coefficients on both sides:
steps.why: The same A·Dr′+B·Dr split used earlier in this chapter, now with the denominator 4cosx+5sinx instead of 4sinx+5cosx — differentiating it swaps which term carries the minus sign.
common_mistakes: Differentiating 4cosx+5sinx as 4sinx+5cosx by confusing which term keeps its sign under differentiation.
Swapping the cosx and sinx coefficient equations.
steps.memory_tip: d/dx(cosx) = −sinx, d/dx(sinx) = +cosx — the minus sign moves to whichever term WAS cosx.

steps.why: The same elimination move as 24.1 — match the B coefficient, subtract to isolate A — but the arithmetic here does not simplify to whole numbers, which is expected, not a warning sign.
common_mistakes: Rounding −2/41 and 23/41 to decimals or 'nicer' fractions, which is not the exact answer.
Sign slip turning 2−(−10/41) into 2−10/41 instead of 2+10/41.
steps.memory_tip: Subtracting a negative ADDS — 2−(−10/41) = 2+10/41, a common slip in this exact line.

steps.label: Substitute back and split the integral
steps.why: With A and B now known fractions, the split into a log term and an x term proceeds exactly as in 24.1, only carrying awkward-looking but exact coefficients through.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to carry the negative sign on A=−2/41 into the log term's coefficient.
Mixing up which fraction (A or B) belongs with the log term and which with the plain x term.
steps.memory_tip: A always pairs with the log term (it multiplied Dr′); B always pairs with the plain x term (it multiplied Dr).

common_mistakes: Dropping the negative sign on the log coefficient in the final line.
Writing 23/41 as a decimal approximation instead of the exact fraction.
steps.memory_tip: The negative sign on A survives all the way to the final boxed line — it is part of the exact answer, not an error.
